title: Elm Education - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Onboarding kickoff to align on project goals, timeline, security requirements (SSO/KMS), and pilot scope for Elm Education's integration with Redwood. AE + SE run through architecture options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), initial benchmarks, and next steps for pilot and SSO setup.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Pilot scope: search + personalized content embeddings
Integration points: LMS, student data pipeline, event ingestion

Schedule SE deep-dive to review data schema and embedding pipeline - target week of 2026-08-17
Customer to confirm pilot dataset and success metrics - due 2026-08-12
Redwood to provision trial Dedicated capacity for benchmark (if requested) and share cost estimate

Carlos Mendez: Prepare initial benchmark template and sample scripts (due: 2026-08-14)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Nguyen (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO - Elm), Liam O'Connor (Head of MLOps - Elm), Dana Park (Eng Manager - Elm), Evan Li (Security - Elm)

[00:00] Sophie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sophie from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Carlos, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya (Elm): Hey Sophie, doing well thanks. Excited to kick this off.
[00:12] Liam (Elm): Afternoon all. We wanted to get alignment on pilot scope and security early.
[00:18] Carlos (Redwood): Yep, that's the plan. We'll walk through the onboarding timeline, integration points with your LMS, and then deep-dive into security - SSO, KMS, audit logs - and then talk deployment options: hosted, dedicated, private.
[00:28] Dana (Elm): Great. Quick note - our timeline is a Q4 pilot, ideally internal pilot in 6 weeks, then wider roll by end of term.
[00:35] Sophie: Okay sounds reasonable. Quick poll for priorities: latency/cost/controls - which is top?
[00:41] Maya: Controls and data residency are first, then predictable latency for student-facing features. Cost is important but secondary.
[00:49] Evan (Elm): From security perspective, SSO with SAML, enterprise KMS for encryption at rest, and detailed audit logs are requirements. We also need retention policies for student PII.
[01:00] Carlos: Understood. Redwood supports SAML SSO, and private deployments can use customer KMS or HSM. For Hosted API we offer encrypted-at-rest with Redwood-managed keys but you can opt into KMS for Private/Dedicated.
[01:15] Sophie: I'll share the security pack after the call - SOC2 summary, encryption notes, and the SSO checklist.
[01:20] Liam: Awesome. On the technical side, we're planning to use embeddings for personalized content search and a reranking layer. We want to understand token costs and inference latency for the student search flow.
[01:32] Carlos: For embeddings, do you have an existing vector DB?
[01:36] Liam: We're using Pinecone for now, but open to alternatives.
[01:39] Carlos: Great - Redwood's embeddings output can integrate with Pinecone, we often see customers pipeline tokens->embeddings->vector store. We also provide guidance on batching and cache TTL to control token costs.
[01:49] Dana: Quick question on Dedicated vs Hosted - what are the tradeoffs?
[01:53] Carlos: Hosted is fastest to ship and fully managed; dedicated gives you reserved capacity with predictable throughput and data isolation; private is for VPC or on-prem when you need complete network control and customer-managed KMS. There's a cost delta but you get SLA and latency guarantees for Dedicated.
[02:08] Maya: For the pilot, would dedicated be overkill?
[02:12] Carlos: Usually for pilots hosted is fine. If you need to run benchmarks against realistic traffic or require KMS/HSM for keys, Dedicated or Private becomes relevant. We can provision short-term dedicated pools for benchmarking.
[02:24] Sophie: We'll include a cost estimate in the deck for both hosted and a 3-month dedicated trial.
[02:29] Evan: About audit logs - can we retain logs for 12 months? We need exports for compliance.
[02:34] Carlos: Yes, Redwood Console has configurable retention. For Private deployments you can push logs to your SIEM. For hosted we support exports and longer retention as an add-on.
[02:44] Liam: On integration, our flow is: LMS events -> ETL -> embedding generation -> vector DB -> API for student search. We need sample code to batch the ETL to reduce cost.
[02:57] Carlos: We have SDK examples for Python and a node sample. Batching, prefix caching, and KV cache re-use will reduce per-token spend. I'll share the benchmark template and a sample script.
[03:10] Dana: Good. Also curious about rollout and guardrails - can we do canary rollouts and A/B tests?
[03:16] Sophie: Yes, Redwood supports A/B and canary with automatic fallbacks, and the Console shows token-level cost and latency per route.
[03:24] Maya: Perfect. A couple of items where we might need clarification: data residency - most of our students are in the EU but we'll have US users too. Can you run in EU region only?
[03:35] Carlos: Yes, we can route inference to EU regions. For strict residency we'd recommend Private or Dedicated pinned to EU region. Hosted can be region-restricted depending on contract.
[03:44] Evan: Also need to know about encryption keys - can Redwood integrate with our Azure Key Vault?
[03:49] Carlos: For Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM; we have integrations for AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault in the enterprise package. I'll note that as an action.
[03:59] Liam: On metrics for pilot success - we want <200ms median latency for search, 95th <500ms, and embedding recall > 0.85 on our eval set.
[04:11] Sophie: Great, we'll build the benchmark to measure those. Carlos, will that be feasible with hosted?
[04:16] Carlos: With right batching and a model choice it's feasible. If not, we can move to Dedicated with optimized kernels and quantization to hit latency cost targets.
[04:29] Maya: What about model options? We want open model support but also safety filters.
[04:33] Carlos: Redwood supports multiple open models and curated image/text models. We also have content filters and can run a safety layer or tool-calling to a moderation service. Model selection will affect latency and cost.
[04:45] Dana: Practical stuff - who will be our primary contact for day-to-day?
[04:49] Sophie: That'll be me for project coordination and Carlos for technical. We'll also loop in CSM once we enter onboarding.
[04:55] Maya: Sounds good. Any blockers from your side today?
[04:58] Liam: We need the SSO checklist and sample embed pipeline; otherwise we can start prepping data.
[05:05] Sophie: Okay noted. We'll send the SSO checklist and onboarding deck today and a security pack by Monday. Carlos will share benchmark scripts and the integration examples.
[05:15] Evan: Minor transcription note - we might want a short runbook for incident response and escalation.
[05:20] Carlos: We'll include the runbook template in the security pack.
[05:25] Sophie: Final recap - next steps are deck + security pack, schedule SE deep-dive week of Aug 17, customer to share pilot dataset and requirements, Redwood to provision trial if needed.
[05:35] Maya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to it.
[05:38] Sophie: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the materials.

End of call.
